name: yara
why: Pattern-matching language for classifying binaries; a real door into malware analysis, though well known in security.

brief.what_it_is: YARA is an open-source pattern-matching tool that malware researchers use to identify and classify samples. You write rules that describe a family, or anything else you want to describe, as a set of textual or binary strings plus a boolean condition over those strings. You point it at files, and it reports which rules match. The homepage says it runs on Windows, Linux and Mac OS X, and it can be driven from the command line or from Python scripts through the yara-python extension. The README's example rule matches files containing any of three strings (two hex byte patterns and one text string) and reports them as silent_banker.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes YARA as 'The pattern matching swiss knife for malware researchers (and everyone else)' and says it is aimed at, but not limited to, helping researchers identify and classify malware samples.
brief.how_it_works: A rule has a meta section, a strings section that names patterns ($a, $b, $c) as hex byte sequences or quoted text, and a condition section with a boolean expression such as '$a or $b or $c'. The homepage says richer rules can use wildcards, case-insensitive strings, regular expressions and other operators, which are covered in the documentation. Rules are applied to files to produce matches.
brief.install_notes: Neither page showed build or install steps. The README says the tool runs on Windows, Linux and Mac OS X, offers a command-line interface, and has a separate yara-python extension for Python use. The homepage also lists a 'Latest release' download and the GitHub repository, which the brief did not fetch. For compressed-file scanning, the homepage recommends the separate yextend extension from Bayshore Networks.
brief.standout: The rule language is the real product: a small, readable, declarative format that many security vendors and sandboxes have adopted, and the homepage lists dozens of organisations using it. The 'swiss knife' framing and the readable example rule make it an approachable way into malware analysis.
brief.status: Maintenance mode, according to an IMPORTANT notice at the top of the GitHub README, which points to the YARA-X project as stable and as the successor. I did not find a last release date or last commit date in the fetched pages, so I cannot give a date from the evidence I saw. The README still lists active CI badges and links to current docs.
brief.caveats: The GitHub README says the project is in maintenance mode and points to YARA-X (https://virustotal.github.io/yara-x/blog/yara-x-is-stable/), so new work is likely to happen there. The homepage lists supported platforms as Windows, Linux and Mac OS X. The brief did not check licensing, the install process, or whether the YARA-X rules are compatible with the classic language. The homepage was reachable, and the GitHub README loaded.
